product_backlog.title: Core To-Do List Management
product_backlog.description: Manage the core to-do lists and their tasks across the application lifecycle.

product_backlog.title: Create a New To-Do List
acceptance_criteria: Given the user is on the main page, When they click 'Create List' and enter a valid name, Then a new to-do list is created and displayed in the application UI.
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can successfully create and view multiple named to-do lists.
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to create a new to-do list with a name so that I can organize my tasks.

acceptance_criteria: Given an existing to-do list, When the user adds a task with a short text description, Then the task appears within that list.
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can add detailed tasks into their created lists.
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to add a task to a list with a short text description so that I can track what needs to be done.
product_backlog.title: Add Task to List
Mark Task as Complete or Incomplete
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can easily update task status and see feedback.
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to mark a task as complete or incomplete so that I can monitor my progress.
acceptance_criteria: Given a task exists in a list, When the user marks the task as complete or incomplete, Then its status toggles accordingly and is reflected in the UI.

product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can clean up individual unwanted tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Given a task exists in a list, When the user deletes the task, Then it is removed from the list and UI.
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to delete a task so that I can remove unwanted items.
product_backlog.title: Delete a Task

product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to delete an entire list and its tasks so that I can remove obsolete categories.
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can delete entire lists along with their nested items.
acceptance_criteria: Given an entire list and its tasks exist, When the user deletes the list, Then the list and all its associated tasks are removed from the application.
product_backlog.title: Delete an Entire List

product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users have clear visual feedback on task completion status.
acceptance_criteria: Given multiple lists with completed and incomplete tasks exist, When the user views all lists, Then completed tasks are visually distinguished from incomplete ones within each list.
product_backlog.title: View All Lists and Visually Distinguish Completed Tasks
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to see all my lists and tasks with completed tasks visually distinguished so that I can easily scan my work.

definition_of_done: specs/ROADMAP.md updated via update_roadmap to reflect this story's completed status
Actual tokens spent logged via log_story_tokens

sprint_backlog.title: Create a New To-Do List
acceptance_criteria: Given the user is on the main page, When they click 'Create List' and enter a valid name, Then a new to-do list is created and displayed in the application UI.
sprint_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can successfully create and view multiple named to-do lists.
sprint_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to create a new to-do list with a name so that I can organize my tasks.
risks_assumptions: Using simple in-memory storage with file backup or simple JSON persistence for robustness across requests within a local session.
Implementing US-0001 through US-0006 in this initial commit/PR since they form the core cohesive MVP feature set of the to-do list app.
dod_checks: App runs successfully and has a web UI
Can create a new to-do list with a name
All acceptance criteria met and tested
tasks: Implement storage model for lists and tasks
Create routes for creating lists, adding tasks, toggling task status, deleting tasks, deleting lists, and viewing all lists
Create HTML template with clean styling and visual distinction for completed tasks
Write unit/integration tests and README with instructions
sprint_backlog.approach: Build a simple Python Flask web application with an in-memory/JSON data structure supporting all core to-do list features (lists and tasks) to satisfy the whole sprint 1 scope (US-0001 through US-0006).
sprint_backlog.test_approach: Manual and automated unit tests using pytest for backend routes and core CRUD operations.

every automated team-performance evaluation run (see `RELEASE.md` "Team performance
evaluation" and `agents/scrum_team/scripts/run_eval.py`). It is intentionally small

## Product Vision

Build a simple to-do list web application. A single user should be able to:

1. Create a new to-do list with a name.
2. Add a task to a list, with a short text description.
3. Mark a task as complete or incomplete.
4. Delete a task.
5. Delete an entire list (and its tasks).
6. See all their lists and, within a list, all its tasks, with completed tasks
   visually distinguished from incomplete ones.

## Constraints (deliberately narrow, to keep this deliverable in 5 sprints)

- **Single user, no authentication.** Do not build login/accounts — out of scope.
- **No persistence requirement beyond the current session/process is assumed** unless
  the team's own design calls for it — persistence approach (in-memory, file, or a
  simple embedded DB) is a legitimate design decision for the team to make and
  justify, not a hidden requirement.
- **A working web UI is required** — the deliverable is something a person could
  open in a browser and actually use, not just a backend API with no way to
  interact with it.
- **No specific language/framework is mandated.** The team should choose something
  it can deliver completely and correctly within budget, and should say why.

## Explicitly out of scope (do not let these creep in)

- Multiple users, sharing, or permissions.
- Due dates, reminders, priorities, tags, or sub-tasks.
- Mobile app, offline support, or real-time sync.
- Any deployment/hosting beyond running locally.

## What "done" looks like after 5 sprints

A person can clone the repo, follow the README, run the app, and actually create a
list, add a few tasks, mark one complete, delete one, and delete a list — end to
end, without reading any code first.
